questions.question: Practical station: Candida krusei.

parts.text: Given broth microdilution. Read MIC.
How would you report susceptibilities?

questions.model_answer: Candida krusei susceptibility reporting: report fluconazole as RESISTANT regardless of the measured MIC - C. krusei is intrinsically fluconazole-resistant, so fluconazole susceptibility testing/breakpoints do not apply to it and it should always be reported resistant. Other azoles (voriconazole) and echinocandins should be interpreted per CLSI species-specific clinical breakpoints for C. krusei based on the actual MIC obtained by broth microdilution; amphotericin B is generally reported using the standard non-species-specific epidemiologic cutoff.
questions.beyond_mandell: CLSI M27/M60 antifungal susceptibility breakpoints for Candida krusei - note: this batch's pagefile (ch237, Rat-Bite Fever) does not match this question's topic (Candida krusei micro), so no page citation is given.

questions.question: 800g infant with NEC on fluconazole prophylaxis and PICC line; develops Candida albicans BSI.

parts.text: What is the drug of choice per IDSA guidelines?
Give three reasons according to the IDSA guidelines why this is preferred.
What other intervention must be done?

cohort_answer.text: Drug of choice: Amphotericin B deoxycholate. Reasons: Most experience in this age group; Patient has been on fluconazole ppx so might be resistant; Well tolerated in this age group; Reaches CNS/urine well. Other intervention: A lumbar puncture and a dilated retinal examination are recommended in neonates with cultures positive for Candida species from blood and/or urine; Removal of CVC; CT or ultrasound imaging of the genitourinary tract, liver, and spleen should be performed if blood cultures are persistently positive for Candida species

questions.question: Candida endocarditis in hemodynamically stable IVDU. TEE shows IE.

parts.text: Name two empiric therapy.
Management other than antifungals or surgery/echo – name two.
Four indications for surgery in IE (other than fungal).

cohort_answer.text: Empiric therapy: Liposomal Ampho B +/- flucytosine or high dose echinocandin. Other management: Dilated retinal exam; Repeat blood culture to document clearance; Removal of CVC. Four indications for surgery in IE: not documented

questions.question:
Q62 (2008)
Farmer presents sick with fever, arthritis, maculopapular rash. 1x2mm non-blanchable rash. 2 weeks ago working in grain bin, acute pain in hand with puncture wounds. Gram stain of wound shows spiral shaped GNB.

parts.text: B) What are 2 organisms that can do this?

questions.question: Farmer presents sick with fever, arthritis, macular-papular rash. 1x2mm non-blanching rash. Two weeks ago was working in grain bin, acute pain in hand with puncture wounds. Gram stain of wound shows spiral shaped bacilli

parts.text: What is the diagnosis?
What are 2 organisms that can do this?
What are 2 treatment options

cohort_answer.text: Streptobacillus moniliformis (rat bite fever) - non-motile spiral GNB, transmitted from rodents via bite/scratch/ingestion, found in North America. Two organisms: Streptobacillus moniliformis, Spirillum minus (found mostly in Asia). Treatment: Penicillin G 2 million q4h x10-14d (alternative doxy or ceftriaxone); wound care; tetanus immunization; consider prophylactic 3 day course of clavulin for rat bites

Q66 (2013 AM, 2015)
What is the gram, catalase (if relevant), confirmatory test for: Strep agalactiae, Proteus vulgaris, Candida albicans, Enterococcus

parts.text: Give gram stain, catalase, and confirmatory test for each organism

cohort_answer.text:
GPC, cat neg, Lancefield antigen test
GNB, cat pos, índole pos, ornithine decarboxylase neg (mirabilis - pos)
Gram pos, cat pos, germ tube positive (dublinensis is the only other pos germ tube)

questions.question: A patient with ALL and a CVC. Blood cultures grow yeast that are germ tube negative.

parts.text: What 2 different antifungal agents could you start empirically (and give mechanisms of action)?
List 2 things to follow-up with in addition to starting antifungals.

cohort_answer.text: Echinocandin – inhibits beta 1,3 D-glucan synthase; Amphotericin B – inhibits ergosterol synthesis which is important to maintain cell wall integrity. (C. krusei – fluconazole resistant, voriconazole/isavuconazole sensitive.) || Removal of CVC, repeat blood culture 24-48 hours after initiating antifungals; Eye exam when neutrophils recover.

questions.question: Explain the resistance mechanism of Candida to fluconazole

parts.text: Explain the resistance mechanism of Candida to fluconazole

questions.model_answer: Candida resistance to fluconazole occurs via: (1) Point mutations in ERG11 (encoding lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, the azole target) that reduce drug binding affinity. (2) Overexpression/upregulation of ERG11, increasing target enzyme quantity. (3) Upregulation of efflux pumps - ABC transporters (CDR1, CDR2) and major facilitator superfamily transporters (MDR1) - that actively pump the drug out of the cell. (4) Alterations in the ergosterol biosynthetic pathway allowing bypass of the blocked step.
questions.beyond_mandell: Standard antifungal resistance mechanism knowledge (mycology/pharmacology, e.g., CID/IDSA reviews).

questions.question: 21. Give Gram stain, colony morphology, catalase (if applicable) and rapid bench ID test and result for: a) Group B Strep; b) Enterococcus spp.; c) Candida albicans; d) Proteus vulgaris

parts.text: a) Group B Strep
b) Enterococcus spp.
c) Candida albicans
d) Proteus vulgaris

cohort_answer.text:
GBS – GPC chains, catalase negative, beta hemolytic, lancefield group B
Enterococcus – GPC pairs/chains, catalase weak positive, alpha or gamma hemolytic, PYR + (GAS too), LAP, bile esculin positive
Candida albicans – "Gram positive" yeast, feet on morphology, germ tube + (also dublinesis), pseudohyphae on wet mount (also with glabrata)
Proteus vulgaris – GNB, catalase +, swarming colony, indole positive, OTC neg (mirabilis +), urease +

questions.question: You are seeing a patient with a pet rat. He likes to play with his rat and gets lots of scratches. He presents now with fever, chills, and fatigue. He has a blood culture return showing a pleomorphic, gram-negative, filamentous rod.

parts.text: What is the syndrome and TWO organisms that cause this syndrome (genus AND species please)
What antibiotic (only 1) can you use to treat?
What are TWO viruses that you could get from rat excrement IN CANADA (specifically said in Canada so no Hantaan or Lassa fever for you)

questions.model_answer:
a) Syndrome: rat-bite fever. Two causative organisms (genus and species): Streptobacillus moniliformis and Spirillum minus.
b) Antibiotic: penicillin (procaine penicillin G, or amoxicillin/ampicillin as an oral option).
c) Two viruses transmissible from rat excreta in Canada: (1) Lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) (2) Seoul orthohantavirus (a rat-borne hantavirus documented in pet and wild rat populations in Canada, distinct from the deer-mouse-borne Sin Nombre virus).
questions.beyond_mandell: Seoul virus in Canadian pet rats reflects public health surveillance reports beyond this chapter excerpt.

questions.question: What are the typical organisms infecting in the following scenarios.

parts.text: Cochlear implants.
Laceration that occurs in a lake
Rat bite in a child who now has fever and rash
Guy competing in a triathlon in South America has fever, high LFTs and conjunctival suffusion

cohort_answer.text: Cochlear implants: meningitis most commonly S. pneumoniae, less often H. influenzae; localized wound infection most commonly S. aureus (also CoNS, streptococci, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, E. coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Achromobacter xylosoxidans, Candida albicans); mastoiditis most commonly S. pneumoniae, S. pyogenes, S. aureus, Pseudomonas spp, H. influenzae. Lake laceration (fresh/brackish water): Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Aeromonas hydrophila, Chromobacterium violaceum (immunosuppression/CGD), Mycobacterium fortuitum, Plesiomonas shigelloides, Edwardsiella tarda, Burkholderia pseudomallei, Streptococcus iniae (fish preparation); salt water: Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae (fish preparation), Mycobacterium marinum, Shewanella spp, Vibrio vulnificus. Rat bite: Streptobacillus moniliformis (most US cases); Spirillum minus (Asia). Triathlon South America: Leptospirosis - abrupt fever, rigors, myalgias, headache after incubation 2-26 days (average 10); conjunctival suffusion important but often overlooked sign (~55% of patients), uncommon in other diseases; subconjunctival hemorrhages also occur.
